*The campus buzzed with electric energy as the Thornehill Thunder prepared for their biggest football rivalry of the season. The stadium roared with school pride, every cheerleader on the sidelines hitting their moves with razor-sharp precision—none more than Ester Figueroa. She flipped her ponytail back, her hips swaying in perfect rhythm to the beat of the band, her cheer uniform hugging every inch of her infamous curves. But even as she kept her routine locked in, her eyes wandered to the quarterback—the golden boy who’d led the Thunder for two seasons straight. That was, until a brutal hit in the second quarter left him sidelined, groaning and motionless on the turf.*

*The crowd fell into nervous silence. But not Ester. She licked her lips and leaned over to whisper to her cheer captain,* “Guess it’s time to see what the backup’s packing.” *Her voice dripped with playful confidence, but even she hadn’t expected what came next. The backup quarterback—some average, quiet-looking guy with barely any buzz to his name—stepped in and turned the entire game on its head. His passes were clean, his footwork tight, and his calm under pressure? Damn near sexy. By the time the final whistle blew and Thornehill secured the win, the crowd lost their minds. So did Ester.* “Alright, mystery boy,” she purred to herself. “You’ve officially earned your spot… on my radar.”

*While the fans stormed the field, Ester slipped away—already knowing exactly where she was headed. The cheerleaders didn’t need her help breaking down. She adjusted her skirt, fluffed her ponytail, and strutted toward the locker rooms like it was her own personal catwalk. Everyone she passed—trainers, teammates, even the assistant coaches—gave her that look. The one that said, they knew. Ester had a reputation. When she came to the locker room after a win, it usually meant one thing. But she wasn’t here for just anyone.*

*She stopped in front of the lockers and leaned against the doorframe, arms crossed under her chest, lips curled in a smirk. The backup QB—still half in uniform, chest rising and falling with post-game adrenaline—froze when he saw her.* “Hey there, champ,” *she said, voice soft but laced with something much heavier.* “I figured someone should properly congratulate you. You just made history tonight.” *He stammered out a thank you, clearly caught off guard. He didn’t know what to make of her, didn’t understand why someone like Ester Figueroa was standing in front of him. So cute, she thought. So… untouched.*

“I’m Ester,” *she added, walking toward him slowly, fingers grazing the locker beside him.* “And I’ve got this rule, y’know… when someone surprises me like that, I don’t just let it slide. I like to… reward greatness.” *The poor guy didn’t know whether to stand his ground or step back. His breath caught when she gently traced her finger along his shoulder pad.*

“Unless you’re scared,” *she teased.* “Are you scared of me, quarterback?”

*He followed her out of the locker room like a man hypnotized, trying not to stare too hard at the sway of her hips or the confident rhythm in her steps. The walk to her dorm was short, but his thoughts were loud. Ester’s room, with its soft pink glow and inviting warmth, seemed to wrap around him the second they stepped inside. She closed the door gently behind him, her smirk never fading. This is what I do, she thought. I give boys their first taste of something unforgettable… and they never walk away the same.*
